q1: You have an important project to start. What's most likely to hold you back?
q1.1: I want to figure out how to do it really well before starting.
q1.2: I imagine how other people might judge the result.
q1.3: I keep thinking about what could go wrong.
q1.4: I'm not sure I have what it takes to do it.
q1.5: I enjoy imagining the finished project more than doing the steps.
q1.6: It feels too big. I have no idea where to begin.
q2: A task has been on your to-do list all week. What best explains the delay?
q2.1: I have so many commitments that I can't find the time.
q2.2: I don't like feeling that someone is forcing me to do it.
q2.3: It doesn't feel urgent enough to make me act yet.
q2.4: I keep choosing something more enjoyable instead.
q2.5: I can't see why doing this really matters to me.
q2.6: The longer I avoid it, the guiltier I feel about returning.
q3: You're working on something and hit a difficult part. What happens?
q3.1: I get caught polishing details instead of moving forward.
q3.2: I'm afraid of making a decision I'll regret.
q3.3: I start imagining a more exciting version of the project.
q3.4: Another commitment interrupts me, and I switch to that.
q3.5: I leave the difficult part until the deadline gets closer.
q3.6: I begin questioning whether the task is worth the effort.
q4: Someone gives you an assignment due Friday. What might get in your way?
q4.1: I worry they won't be happy with what I produce.
q4.2: I'm not confident I can complete it successfully.
q4.3: There are so many parts that I can't decide what to tackle first.
q4.4: Being told what to do makes me want to resist.
q4.5: I keep taking fun little breaks that turn into long ones.
q4.6: Once I fall behind, I feel too guilty to face the assignment.
q5: You're supposed to share your work with others. What's hardest?
q5.1: I keep finding things I want to improve first.
q5.2: I worry about criticism, embarrassment, or disapproval.
q5.3: I've been too busy with other commitments to prepare.
q5.4: I dislike having to share it on someone else's terms.
q5.5: I'm not convinced sharing it serves a meaningful goal.
q5.6: I've already delayed so much that I feel embarrassed to show it.
q6: You finally have a free afternoon. Why might you still put things off?
q6.1: I can't decide what to do without worrying about the outcome.
q6.2: I doubt I'll be able to make worthwhile progress.
q6.3: I get lost thinking about possibilities instead of taking action.
q6.4: There are too many things on my mind to pick just one.
q6.5: Without a deadline, I can't seem to activate my focus.
q6.6: Doing something enjoyable right now feels much more appealing.
q7: You've made a little progress, but there's still more to do. What happens?
q7.1: My progress doesn't feel meaningful because the result isn't good enough.
q7.2: Seeing what's left makes me doubt my ability to finish.
q7.3: The remaining steps blur together, and I freeze.
q7.4: I move on to other responsibilities I've agreed to handle.
q7.5: I reward myself with a distraction and forget to return.
q7.6: I criticize myself for not doing more, then avoid continuing.
q8: You're given a vague task with little guidance. What do you tend to do?
q8.1: I keep trying to guess what would impress the person who assigned it.
q8.2: I spend time trying to eliminate every possible risk.
q8.3: I brainstorm ambitious ideas without testing a small one.
q8.4: I feel resistant to following directions I didn't choose.
q8.5: I wait until time pressure forces me to make a move.
q8.6: I struggle to care because I don't see a personal reason for doing it.
q9: You planned to get something done today, but it's now evening. What happened?
q9.1: I spent too much time preparing, researching, or refining.
q9.2: I got carried away thinking about ideas instead of executing them.
q9.3: Everything felt equally important, so I barely started.
q9.4: I avoided an obligation that felt imposed on me.
q9.5: I assumed I'd become productive when the deadline was closer.
q9.6: After a slow start, I felt bad about myself and stopped trying.
q10: When you choose between an important task and something else, what usually pulls you away?
q10.1: Thinking about how my work will be judged.
q10.2: Thinking about negative outcomes and uncertain consequences.
q10.3: Feeling that I'm not capable enough to succeed.
q10.4: Other people's requests and commitments I've already made.
q10.5: Something fun that makes me feel good immediately.
q10.6: Feeling disconnected from the reason I should do the task.
a1.name: The Perfectionist
a1.desc: Your brain wants everything to be just right. Sometimes, that makes starting the hardest part.
a1.thought: If I can't do it perfectly, why even start?
a1.help: Permission to make a rough first version, with no polishing.
a2.name: The Approval Seeker
a2.desc: You care deeply about others. Worrying about their reactions can make sharing your work feel bigger than it is.
a2.thought: What if people think I'm not good enough?
a2.help: Sharing a small draft with one trusted person, on my own terms.
a3.name: The Worrier
a3.desc: Your mind is good at spotting possibilities, including the scary ones. A small safe experiment can help you move.
a3.root: Fear of uncertainty and negative outcomes.
a3.help: A tiny, reversible experiment that doesn't need certainty.
a4.name: The Self-Doubter
a4.desc: You might underestimate what you're capable of. Little pieces of evidence can help your confidence catch up.
a4.thought: I probably can't do this anyway.
a4.help: One small achievable action that reminds me I can make progress.
a5.name: The Dreamer
a5.desc: Your imagination is a wonderful place. A tiny concrete step can bring one of those big ideas into the real world.
a5.root: Difficulty translating ideas into concrete actions.
a5.thought: I have an amazing idea! I'll figure out the details later.
a5.help: Turning one idea into a specific action I can do in five minutes.
a6.name: The Overwhelmed One
a6.desc: When everything feels important, choosing anything can feel impossible. You only need one next step.
a6.thought: There are so many things to do. Where do I even begin?
a6.help: Hiding the big list and choosing just one manageable next step.
a7.name: The Overdoer
a7.desc: You're generous with your time. Leaving a little space for yourself makes your own important things possible.
a7.thought: I'll just take on one more thing.
a7.help: Protecting a small window of time and setting one boundary.
a8.name: The Defier
a8.desc: Your independence matters to you. Finding your own reason to act can turn an obligation into a choice.
a8.thought: I hate being told what to do.
a8.help: Choosing my own reason, approach, and first step.
a9.name: The Crisis-Maker
a9.desc: A ticking clock can switch your focus on. Small early milestones can create momentum without the last-minute rush.
a9.help: A short timer and an early milestone that creates momentum now.
a10.name: The Instant-Gratification Chaser
a10.desc: Your brain loves a reward right now. Tiny focus sessions and immediate little celebrations can work with that.
a10.root: Preference for immediate rewards over delayed benefits.
a10.help: Putting one distraction away and earning a small reward after two minutes.
a11.name: The Purpose Drifter
a11.desc: Meaning matters to you. Connecting a task to something you actually care about can make the next step lighter.
a11.root: Weak connection between tasks and personal values.
a11.thought: Why am I even doing this?
a11.help: Connecting a small action to a value I actually care about.
a12.name: The Shame Spiraler
a12.desc: Feeling bad about a delay can make returning even harder. A kind restart counts, no matter what happened earlier.
a12.thought: I've already wasted the whole day.
a12.help: A guilt-free restart and recognizing one thing I already tried.

coach.crisis: I’m glad you told me. You deserve real support right now. If you might hurt yourself, contact local emergency services or a crisis line (US/Canada: call or text 988). Can you reach someone you trust to stay with you?
coach.guilt: A slow start doesn’t cancel the rest of your day. You don’t have to earn a fresh start. What is one small thing you did manage, even if it was just trying?
coach.perfect: Let’s give this a finish line instead of an endless improvement loop. Name one thing that would make this useful, even if it isn’t perfect. What would ‘good enough’ look like?
coach.break: Let’s make this smaller: 1) Open the place where the work happens. 2) Write down one concrete next action. 3) Try that action for five minutes. You can customize these in Tiny Mission Builder. What goal are we shrinking?
coach.rest: Rest can be a real need, not a failure to try. Could you choose between a short break and one very small action, based on your energy right now?
coach.action: Thanks for naming it. Try this: open what you need, create one rough line or example, and stop after two minutes if you want. You can use The Messy Start to practice. What is the smallest visible action you could take?
coach.try: That gives you something concrete to work with. Keep it small enough for the energy you have, and let an attempt count. Would you like to try it now with a short challenge?
coach.default: You don’t need to solve the whole thing right now. Let’s find one tiny beginning. What’s the task you’re avoiding?
coach.pattern: Your {name} pattern suggests that a little less pressure may help. You don’t need to solve the whole thing right now. Let’s find one tiny beginning. What’s the task you’re avoiding?
